The bamboo sole Heteromycteris japonicus is a small flatfish species inhabiting coastal waters of the northwestern Pacific. Field surveys indicate that individuals attain a maximum total length of 15.8 cm [Li = 15.8 cm], a modest size characteristic of many soleid fishes inhabiting shallow sandy substrates. At a sustained water temperature of 17.5 °C [T = 17.5 °C], the incubation period for developing embryos lasts approximately 8.5 days [ab = approximately 8.5 days], after which the prolarvae emerge from the chorion. The newly hatched yolk-sac larvae possess a minimal wet weight at birth of 0.00014 grams [Wwb = 0.00014 grams], reflecting the small egg size typical of this genus. This lecithotrophic stage depends entirely on endogenous yolk reserves until the onset of exogenous feeding, which occurs shortly after the mouth becomes functional.

Sexual maturation in this species begins when individuals reach a total length at puberty of 7 cm [Lp = 7 cm], a threshold that typically corresponds to an approximate age of one to two years under natural conditions. The corresponding wet weight at puberty is 3.8 grams [Wwp = 3.8 grams], a value derived from length-weight relationships established for the population. At the peak of the spawning season, the gonadosomatic index (GSI) reached approximately 10% [GSI = approximately 10%] when measured at 17.5 °C [T = 17.5 °C]. This index is comparable to values reported for other small-bodied pleuronectiforms and suggests a strategy of producing multiple batches of pelagic eggs over an extended spawning period that spans the warmer months.

Growth trajectory analyses reveal that the ultimate wet weight for bamboo sole reaches 46.7 grams [Wwi = 46.7 grams], which is achieved near the maximum recorded total length of the species. The length-weight relationship follows a positive allometric pattern wherein mass increases disproportionately with length, a common feature among flatfishes that undergo significant changes in body depth during post-settlement development. Juvenile individuals recruit to benthic habitats following larval metamorphosis, during which the characteristic ocular migration occurs. Post-settlement juveniles display rapid somatic growth during their first year, gradually decelerating as they approach the asymptotic size. The comparatively moderate ultimate body mass of this species reflects its occupation of a relatively low trophic position within coastal sandy-bottom communities.

The maximum lifespan recorded for bamboo sole under natural conditions in the Tagus estuary, where the average annual water temperature is 17.5 °C [T = 17.5 °C], is approximately 12 years [am = approximately 12 years]. This longevity is relatively extended for a flatfish of its size and may be linked to the species' iteroparous reproductive strategy, which spreads reproductive effort across multiple consecutive spawning seasons. Age determination based on otolith ring counts from field-collected specimens consistently supports this estimate, with the oldest individuals exhibiting well-defined annuli that correspond to a lifespan of 4380 days. Such longevity allows multiple reproductive opportunities and contributes to population stability despite potentially variable recruitment success in fluctuating coastal environments.

The species exhibits a nocturnal activity pattern, emerging from shallow burial in sandy substrates to forage on small benthic invertebrates. This developmental rate is consistent with the species' overall life-history strategy that balances small initial size with extended adult longevity.
